classification.difficultyReason: Discover the angular pigeonhole argument at a vertex, use the cosine rule to compare endpoint distances, and rule out both possible directions of a nearest-point connection.

content.prompt: Suppose a set of points in the plane is such that the distance between any pair of these points is distinct. Prove that when each point is connected by a line segment to the point that is closest to it that no point is connected to more than five other points.

answer.short:
No point can be connected to six or more other points.

Two incident segments would form an angle at most $60^\circ$. The cosine rule makes the farther endpoint closer to the other endpoint than to the common point, contradicting the nearest-point connections.
answer.worked:
Suppose a point $A$ is connected to at least six other points. Two consecutive incident segments, $AB$ and $AC$, form an angle $\theta\leq60^\circ$, since the angles around $A$ sum to $360^\circ$.

Write $AB=b$ and $AC=c$, labelling the endpoints so that $b>c$; the distances are distinct. By the cosine rule,
$$\begin{align*}BC^2&=b^2+c^2-2bc\cos\theta\\BC^2&\leq b^2+c^2-2bc\cos60^\circ\\BC^2&\leq b^2+c^2-bc\\BC^2&\leq b^2+c(c-b)\\BC^2&<b^2.\end{align*}$$
Thus $BC<BA$, so $B$ cannot choose $A$ as its closest point. Also $AC<AB$, so $A$ cannot choose $B$ as its closest point. Therefore the segment $AB$ cannot be present, a contradiction. Hence every point is connected to at most five other points.
